==English==

===Etymology===
From {{m|en|free|Free|not enslaved}} {{m|en|issue|Issue|progeny}}, "an antiquated designation for descendants of enslaved people who were freed before the Civil War", later applied to Monacans because Virginia laws for a time required births to be registered as either "White" or "Colored", erasing Indians, and clerks later haphazardly classified Monacans (even from the same mother and father) as "Mixed Indian", "Negro", or "Issue".<ref>'''2022''' March 16, "[https://www.washingtonpost.com/history/2022/03/16/monacan-rassawek-resolution/ Monacan Indian Nation defeats utility project at historic capital of Rassawek]", ''The Washington Post''</ref><ref>Karenne Wood and Diane Shields, "[https://web.archive.org/web/20231117180604/https://www.monacannation.com/step-back-in-time.html Historical Chronology of the Monacan Indian Nation]"</ref>

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɪʃ(j)u/|/ˈɪʃ(j)ə/}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|derogatory}} A [[Monacan]] Indian; a member of a [[Mestee]] group originating in Amherst County, [[Virginia]].
